note: Reel 16: Diwali's Missing Colour. Every colour in a firework is a burning metal (strontium red, calcium orange, sodium yellow, barium green: PBS NOVA). Blue comes from copper, and copper's blue is fragile: too hot and it washes out to white (PBS NOVA), too cool and it is too faint; makers add chlorine donors, sometimes plastic (PVC), so the copper chloride that glows blue can form; a perfect blue is 'the holy grail' of fireworks (PBS NOVA). India's twist: in 2018 the Supreme Court barred barium salts in firecrackers (order of 31 Oct 2018: 'barium salts in the manufacture of firecrackers will not be used'), and barium makes green; 'green crackers' (CSIR-NEERI) are green for lower pollution, not colour. Facts: docs/research.md. Kokoro af_heart, speed 1.0. 'Diwali' in Hindi is दिवाली [d̪iʋaːliː], 'di-VAA-lee': s01 and s14 are planned by hand; s01b/s14b (long first i) and s01c/s14c (the plain spelling, Kokoro's own plan) are there for the ears to judge. Round 2 (run 41192804375): 'too faint to see' was heard as 'too fantasy' by every ear in every take: s07 is now 'Too cool, and it barely glows.' at 0.95; s12's 'barium in crackers' was heard 'barium and crackers' by small.en: now 'banned barium from firecrackers'. Diwali: the ears chose /dɪvˈɑːli/ ('d ɪ v ɑː l i', di-VAA-lee); Kokoro's own plan was 'duh-WAH-lee'.

lines.text: Too cool, and it barely glows.
In two thousand eighteen, India's Supreme Court banned barium from firecrackers. Barium makes green.
